title: Expose local API (or browser-accessible UI) for AI agent automation
body:
AI Job Hunter is currently a Tauri desktop app — a native window with no way for an AI agent (browser-automation tools only) to read or interact with it. To let an AI assistant operate it reliably, we need one of two things, in order of preference:

## Option A (preferred): Local HTTP API

Expose a localhost-only HTTP API the app already has the data for, so an agent can query it directly instead of trying to read pixels off a window.

- Bind to `127.0.0.1` only (not `0.0.0.0`) — no external exposure.
- Protect it with a local token (e.g. written to a file in the app's own AppData folder at startup, like `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI Job Hunter\api-token.txt`) so only local processes with file access can call it.
- Read-only endpoints to start:
  - `GET /api/best-matches` → list of matched jobs (id, title, company, location, match score, date found, short description)
  - `GET /api/jobs/{id}` → full job detail (description, requirements, application URL/route, source)
  - `GET /api/profile` → current CV/profile summary being matched against
  - `GET /api/automations` → list of configured automations and their status
- Serve a machine-readable schema at `GET /api/openapi.json` so an agent can self-discover endpoints instead of hardcoding them.
- **No auto-submit/auto-apply endpoint.** Application submission should stay a manual, human-approved step — the API is for discovery/evaluation data only, not for triggering irreversible actions.

## Option B (fallback): Browser-accessible UI

If the API is a bigger lift right now, an interim option is running the existing frontend as a normal local web page (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:PORT`), using the same localhost-only + token-gated access. That alone would let an agent navigate it with standard browser automation, no native window access needed.

Either option unblocks reliable automation; Option A is more robust long-term since UI automation is brittle against redesigns, while an API is stable and explicit about what an agent can and can't do.
